hook_text: Nobody feeds the spinach in this garden. So how does it grow so big?
clip_script: A school garden in Thohoyandou. Spinach, beans, maize. Nobody feeds them, but they grow and grow. Because green plants are food factories. Roots pull up water. Tiny holes in the leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air. Green chlorophyll catches sunlight. Out comes sugar, food for the plant, and oxygen, a gift for us to breathe. Put a bean plant in a dark cupboard, and it turns pale and weak. No light, no food.
visual_style: Whiteboard leaf as a little factory with arrows: water in, carbon dioxide in, sunlight in, sugar and oxygen out.
mood: Wonder and discovery, like finding a secret machine.
pacing: Question, three raw materials, two products, then the dark cupboard test.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and set up your own bean plant test.
